newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong Motor in talks with GM - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong Motor in talks with GM - paper.

text.p: South Korea's Ssangyong Motor Co is discussing a $300 million capital investment this year with General Motors Corp and other foreign firms, a leading business newspaper reported on Thursday.
The Korea Economic Daily report quoted an unidentified official at Ssangyong Motor's parent Ssangyong Group as saying that negotiations would be concluded by June.
Ssangyong Motor is a joint venture between the Ssangyong Group and Germany's Mercedes Benz, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG .
The deal with General Motors was a core part of Ssangyong's plan to reduce its debt-to-equity ratio to about 1,000 percent from 10,000 percent at the end of 1996, the report said.
Ssangyong officials were not immediately available for comment.
Ssangyong Motor, which specialises in making four wheel-drive vehicles and trucks, has said it would sell off its headquarters building and other assets to cut the debt burden.
In March, the company said it would allow foreigners to hold up to 49 percent of the company.
Ssangyong Motor posted a net loss of 228.49 billion won in 1996, up from the previous year's 126.23 billion won loss.
